subject: Differentiated SLA request — live stream vs sync endpoints (TTFT + tokens/sec)
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@streamlinelabs.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, procurement@streamlinelabs.com
Date: 2028-11-29T09:13:00-08:00
Subject: SLA needs for Live Stream ingestion — initial ask

Jordan / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Streamline Labs is preparing a pilot that will ingest real-time transcripts and render tokens to our client UIs as they arrive. A couple of asks from engineering/procurement as we scope commercial terms: 

- Can Redwood provide a differentiated SLA for live streaming endpoints vs the standard sync endpoints? Specifically we need guarantees for time-to-first-token (TTFT) and sustained token/s throughput for a pooled session model.
- Target we have in mind: TTFT <= 400ms for 99.9% of streaming requests, and sustained 200 tokens/sec per stream for 95% during normal production.
- If dedicated capacity is required for that profile, please quantify additional cost and any lead time.
- We'll also need a fallback behavior defined — if the streaming pool is overloaded, what does the client see and what credits are applied?

Attached is our rough traffic matrix and pilot timelines (streamline-sla-request-ttft-tokens.xlsx). Procurement is on copy for contract planning. Can you confirm feasibility and next steps?

Thanks,
Alex Mercer
Head of Platform Engineering
Streamline Labs

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@streamlinelabs.com>, procurement@streamlinelabs.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-11-29T12:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA needs for Live Stream ingestion — initial ask

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. We're excited to work through this. High level response: yes, we can offer differentiated SLAs for streaming vs sync endpoints, but there are a couple of tradeoffs and operational controls we need to agree on.

Quick summary of options we can propose:

1) Dedicated streaming pool (recommended for strongest guarantees)
   - TTFT target: 150–300ms  (99.9) depending on model & seq-length distribution
   - Sustained tokens/sec: configurable, typical guarantee 150–250 tokens/sec per stream on dedicated pools
   - Pricing: premium over committed capacity (we'll quantify in follow-up)

2) Hybrid: reserved baseline + burst shared pool
   - Lower base cost, slightly looser TTFT during bursts (up to 500ms), automated fallback to sync endpoint when overloaded

3) Hosted-synchronous endpoints (no streaming guarantees)
   - Standard TTFT/throughput profile per our public SLOs

Next steps I recommend: schedule a short architecture call with our SRE/Serving team so we can map Streamline's traffic matrix to an actual capacity plan. Marissa, can you pick times?

I'll also loop in Karthik and Soojin — we need engineering to confirm fallback semantics & compensation.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@streamlinelabs.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: 2028-12-01T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA needs for Live Stream ingestion — technical proposal

Alex, Jordan — following our internal sizing sync, here's a technical proposal that maps to Streamline's ask and outlines options, fallback behavior, and measurable remedies.

Proposal (concise):

- Baseline offer (Hybrid reserved + burst):
  * TTFT: 99th pct median 120ms, 99.9th pct bounded at 400ms during steady-state on reserved baseline. During burst, TTFT may increase up to 700ms for 0.1% of requests before failover.
  * Sustained tokens/sec: guaranteed 150 tokens/sec per stream at 95% percentile on reserved capacity. Burst pool provides additional capacity but without percentile guarantees.
  * Fallback: when both reserved + burst exhausted we route to sync endpoint (non-streaming) which will return complete payloads; client sees a single consolidated response. We mark those requests in logs and apply SLA credits per contract.

- Premium offer (Dedicated streaming pool):
  * TTFT: 99.9% <= 300ms for common open-source models we benchmarked. With model finetunes/long-context, plan will be adjusted.
  * Sustained tokens/sec: contractual guarantee 200 tokens/sec per stream (95%) with enforced pre-provisioned GPU slices.
  * Fallback: buffered edge-delivery + graceful degrade (partial chunks delivered) with automatic failover to alternate region/pool before switching to sync.

Operational controls & mitigations we propose:
- Prefix caching for repeated prompts to reduce effective TTFT for common flows
- Socket pre-warm and keepalive tuning for long-lived sessions
- Model variant routing (lighter quantized model during extreme load) — documented and opt-in
- Burst protection and token-throttling guardrails (to protect other tenants)

Compensation / credits:
- If TTFT/Sustained tokens guarantees are missed for reserved baseline: credit = pro rata % of monthly committed fees tied to number of violations (example calculation attached in PDF).
- For dedicated pools we offer higher SLAs and smaller credit bands but require minimum committed spend and 30-day provisioning notice.

Attachment: redwood-sla-diff-proposal.pdf (includes sample SLO tables, measurement windows, and an example credit calc).

Questions for Streamline:
1) For pilot sizing — confirm 95th/99th percentile message sizes and expected concurrent streams.
2) Do you need cross-region failover? If yes, we should include region-specific dedicated capacity.
3) Are you prepared to accept model-variant routing (quantized fallback) during extreme load?

I'll plan to send a firm pricing delta after we have the traffic matrix answers.

-Karthik
Principal, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@streamlinelabs.com>, jordan_blake@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com, procurement@streamlinelabs.com
Date: 2028-12-02T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA needs for Live Stream ingestion — next steps and pricing delta

Alex — thanks for the quick collaboration. Based on Karthik's proposal and your attached traffic matrix, here's a pragmatic path for the pilot and commercial terms.

Pilot offer (30 days):
- Dedicated streaming pool (pilot) sized for 500 concurrent streams.
- Measured guardrails: TTFT 99.9% <= 350ms, sustained tokens/sec guarantee 180 tokens/sec (95%).
- Price: pilot add-on = +18% on committed GPU equivalent for the duration of the pilot (we'll convert to exact $ in the SOW).
- Compensation: if we miss agreed SLOs, apply a 10% credit on pilot add-on fee for each measurement window breach (up to 50% cap).

Production path (post-pilot):
- Option A: Continue dedicated pools with contractual guarantees (minimum 6-mo commit).
- Option B: Move to hybrid reserved + burst with documented credits & dynamic routing.

Action items:
- Jordan: please share the updated SOW template and HubSpot record id. (HS-987654321)
- Alex: please confirm concurrent stream target and whether you want cross-region failover.
- Procurement: we'll circulate a short amendment covering pilot pricing & credit mechanics; expect DocuSign link.

I'll loop Legal on the amendment early next week but wanted to get alignment on the technical/pricing front now so procurement has clear numbers.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
